known_fake_reports.summary: Toronto Police Financial Crimes: at least 3 recent cases of fake QR stickers on on-street meters; one victim expecting to pay $7 was charged almost $2,000. Also fake QR codes on Bike Share Toronto bikes. No domains named.

Green P alert: older machines have no QR capability, so any sticker is fraudulent; new machines show the QR built into the screen; use the Green P app. City of Toronto repeats this on its parking page.

Independent blog: 'Scan to Pay' sticker placed over the real on-screen code on new meters along Yonge St led to a fake Green P-style payment page; later stickers smaller, with payment-processor logos, using a QR redirect service.

cities.research_notes: Only Green P domains (greenp.com + subdomains) are official for City/TPA parking. Any QR on a STICKER on a Green P machine is fake per Green P. City is reviewing its 2,700 on-street meters as app use grows. A 2024 CBC story (cbc.ca/1.7291281) could not be read.
